snippet.description:

snippet.title: 5 Grocery Store Foods For Long Term Storage - No Repackaging Required
snippet.description:
Long-term food storage doesn’t have to mean Mylar bags, oxygen absorbers, vacuum sealers, buckets and complicated repackaging.

In this video, I’m looking at 5 types of grocery-store foods you can buy, bring home and put directly onto your storage shelves — no repackaging required.

We’ll look at:
• Properly packaged nuts
• Canned foods
• Freeze-dried meals
• Peanut butter and other nut butters
• Shelf-stable dairy products

Some of these foods are rotation foods that may give you a few years of storage, while others can potentially last for decades.

The goal isn’t to make every food last 20 or 30 years. It’s to understand which foods actually benefit from repackaging — and which ones are better left in the package they came in.
If you’re new to emergency food storage and want a simple place to start, these five categories can give you plenty of options without all the extra equipment.

What grocery-store food do you store long-term without repackaging? Let me know in the comments.

snippet.description:
🔗 The complete Amish Home System — cut every household bill to zero:
https://eliyodersecrets.com

https://youtu.be/7NuzJUwhuBE

In a Holmes County, Ohio root cellar, on shelves a man named Eli built in nineteen eighty-four, there are eighteen blue cylinders of plain white salt lined up next to twelve plastic gallons of white vinegar, a wooden crate holding three hundred paraffin emergency candles, and two hundred boxes of strike-anywhere matches — and the family that owns the cellar has not run out of food, light, soap, or medicine in forty-one years of marriage. A twenty-six ounce blue cylinder of plain non-iodized salt at any Walmart costs one dollar and forty-seven cents and preserves roughly twenty pounds of pork shoulder indefinitely. A plastic gallan of white vinegar costs three dollars and twenty-four cents and pickles cabbage that stays edible on a pantry shelf for two years. A one-pound box of baking soda costs under a dollar and replaces six different products under the average American sink. A box of one hundred and twenty paraffin emergency candles costs four dollars and ninety cents and raises the temperature of a closed bedroom by three degrees Fahrenheit per candle. A queen-sized fleece blanket costs four dollars and eighty-eight cents and lets a homeowner drop the nighttime thermostat from sixty-eight to fifty-five without losing sleep. And when you combine these eleven items using methods the Amish have been refining since the first Anabaptist families landed in Philadelphia in seventeen thirty-seven, you eliminate the need to ever pay another six-hundred-dollar annual cleaning supply bill, four-hundred-dollar winter heating bill, or three-hundred-dollar prescription cough medicine bill — without permits, without contractors, and without modifying anything in the house already standing on your property.

In nineteen forty-two, the United States Department of Agriculture published a bulletin explaining that one pound of plain white salt could preserve roughly ten pounds of pork shoulder indefinitely without refrigeration. The Anabaptist farmers of the Alsace region had been doing this since the sixteen hundreds. Pennsylvania Dutch sauerkraut, fermented in stoneware crocks with nothing but cabbage and salt, has been keeping families fed through European and American winters since the seventeen twenties. The Ordnung — the unwritten rules of Amish living — has stated since eighteen sixty-five that a household should be able to feed itself for one year without leaving the property. Buried in the archives of the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission, cataloged under the title Folk Medicine of the Pennsylvania Germans, written in nineteen thirty-five by a researcher named Thomas Brendle, there is a documented account of dozens of cases going back to the eighteen twenties in which Amish and Mennonite settlers used dried mullein leaves — the tall yellow flowering weed that grows wild on every roadside in America — mixed with plain table salt as a chest poultice for severe respiratory illness.

In nineteen forty-two, the United States Department of Agriculture published a bulletin explaining that one pound of plain white salt could preserve roughly ten pounds of pork shoulder indefinitely without refrigeration. The Anabaptist farmers of the Alsace region had been doing this since the sixteen hundreds. Pennsylvania Dutch sauerkraut, fermented in stoneware crocks with nothing but cabbage and salt, has been keeping families fed through European and American winters since the seventeen twenties. snippet.title: Electricity Crisis: लोगों का प्रदर्शन, रैपिड रेल बंद, पटरी पर चले लोग, Video Viral
snippet.description:
*THE NORTH INDIA ELECTRICITY CRISIS GETTING WORSE BY THE DAY*

*By Saurabh Shukla*

North India is suffocating under an unprecedented power collapse. 

The power department has vanished. Citizens are pushed to their absolute limits as scorching heat waves meet completely dark, lifeless grids.

*VIDEO HIGHLIGHTS:*

🔹 Rapid Metro stops mid-track in Gurugram. 
🔹 Stranded passengers walk on elevated tracks. 
🔹 Hospitals run out of backup electricity. 🔹 Angry citizens block major national highways.

*Is privatization failing to secure basic public needs?*

[01:18] MASSIVE GURUGRAM BLACKOUT A fire at a local sector transformer triggered absolute panic. The Rapid Metro grid failed instantly. Trapped passengers suffocated inside dark coaches before forcing open the emergency exits.

"यात्री पटरी पर मेट्रो की पटरी पर पैदल चलते हुए नजर आते हैं क्योंकि ना मेट्रो आगे जाएगी ना पीछे जाएगी बड़ी मुश्किल से दरवाजे खुले तो यह बाहर निकले अंदर बिजली जाने से ना एसी था सफोकेटिंग हो गया था इनके लिए जान पर बनाई थी सांस नहीं आ रही थी" [01:18]

[03:31] HOSPITALS ON THE EDGE 

The crisis has entered critical emergency zones across Uttar Pradesh. 

Intensive care units and life-saving ventilators are failing. Doctors are forced to scramble for erratic diesel generators to save patients.

"अस्पतालों में बिजली चली गई है अस्पतालों में वेंटिलेटर्स और आईसीयू चलाने तक की नौबत आ रही है कि मतलब कैसे चलाएं जनरेटर का इंतजाम किया जा रहा है" [03:31]

[04:14] HIGHWAYS BLOCKED IN ANGER 

Furious with endless blackouts and zero voltage, citizens have taken over the streets. 

The vital Lucknow-Kanpur highway was completely choked by protestors. 

The double-engine governance promises have totally crashed on the ground.

"बिजली कटौती की वजह से लोग इतना परेशान हो गए कि उन्होंने कल रात लखनऊ कानपुर हाईवे जाम कर दिया और फिर वहां पर पुलिस को आकर के लखनऊ कानपुर हाईवे को खुलवाना पड़ा लोगों ने कहा कि वह बेहद परेशान है कई-कई दिन से बिजली नहीं आ रही है" [04:14]

[05:37] *GROUND WORKERS UNDER PRESSURE*

Local power offices are facing massive public outrage. 

Angry crowds are directly cornering junior engineers. 

Political leaders urge citizens not to blame contract workers who face intense systemic pressure.

"भाजपा की गलत नीतियों की वजह से उत्तर प्रदेश में जो असहनीय बिजली संकट चल रहा है उसके लिए बिजली विभाग के कनिष्ठ कर्मचारियों या लाइनमैनों पर जनता अपना गुस्सा ना निकाले" [09:10]

[12:09] *THE SELF-RELIANT CITIZEN* 

The government demands timely digital payments and installs smart meters. 

Yet it fails to provide basic infrastructure. Citizens are sarcastically left to buy hand fans to survive the grueling summer nights.

"तो बिजली की कटौती बेरोजगारी ये सब आत्मनिर्भर बनाने के लिए बिजली पेपर लीक ये सब आत्मनिर्भर तो सब आत्मनिर्भर हो जाइए तो अपना हाथ वाला पंखा लीजिए उसको डुलाइए नहीं तो अखबार लीजिए उसको डुलाइए" [12:09]

Systemic failure to forecast seasonal summer demand proves that aggressive privatization without strong state accountability leaves citizens completely stranded.

snippet.description:
What are the most important bug out bag essentials everyone should have? In this video, I go through the critical items I believe belong in every bug out bag and explain why each one matters in a 72-hour emergency or evacuation.

A bug out bag is essentially a small, portable preparedness kit designed to help you handle the basics when you're away from home and your normal emergency supplies. We'll cover water and purification, emergency food, shelter and clothing, first aid supplies, fire-starting tools, cordage and paracord, a metal container for cooking and boiling water, cutting tools, emergency lighting, and quality footwear.

But putting together the best bug out bag isn't just about buying survival gear. Once the fundamentals are covered, your bag should be customized around your environment, climate, planned destination, bug out route, available resources and your own personal needs.

I also explain why you should actually practice carrying your bug out bag, pay attention to its total weight, and keep it somewhere accessible. A perfectly stocked emergency bag won't do much good sitting in a closet when you're miles away from home.

Whether you're building your first 72-hour kit, updating an existing bug out bag, or looking for ideas for your emergency preparedness gear, this video covers the core supplies I think you should start with before adding anything else.
